correctness.rationale: The commutator is the standard nondegenerate F_q-valued alternating form. For K>=Z with additive image U, centralization depends only on the F_q-span S of U, so C(K)/Z=S^perp. Writing s=dim_Fp U and d=dim_Fq S gives the exact measure q^(2n+2)p^(s-fd); s<=fd with equality exactly for F_q-linear U. For arbitrary K, adjoining Z leaves the centralizer unchanged and can only increase the measure, proving the global maximum and equality conditions. Double orthogonality gives every F_q-subspace as a centralizer. The nonprime-field monotonicity failure is witnessed explicitly by Z<pi^-1(F_p v).

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete lattice, not just a scalar measure, for a standard infinite family. It explains exactly how the known quasi-antichain at Heisenberg rank one grows into the full finite-geometry subspace lattice at higher rank, and it sharply separates centralizer-lattice monotonicity from full subgroup-lattice monotonicity according to whether the field is prime. The explicit measure defect p^(s-fd) quantifies how non-F_q-linear additive subgroups fall below the maximum and is reusable in subsequent subgroup-lattice questions.
